problems: All five TF links rely on in-vitro QBiC-SELEX predictions, not demonstrated occupancy at this variant in adipose cells; the binding grades therefore remain weak.

The cCRE overlap is established, but E05 leaves its activity in the supplied adipose proxy context unknown. Element-to-gene contacts are from other biosamples, and L2G is prioritization rather than a causal perturbation.

E27 is a tested-negative result for a significant adipose-subcutaneous eQTL. It weakens support for adipose-specific expression mediation, but does not negate the cautious claims or FTO's relative L2G prioritization.

The predicted binding directions do not establish the direction of a transcriptional effect. In particular, H3 predicts stronger binding to C although T is the reported risk allele; no cited evidence connects that affinity change to gene expression or disease direction.
E25 and E26 are not-tested results for adipose ChIP-seq; their absence of matching experiments or ReMap peaks must not be treated as evidence against GATA2 or PRRX1 binding.

checks.why: A variant-overlapping GATA2 peak in an adipose biosample would strengthen the case for GATA2-specific occupancy; its absence would leave the family-level in-vitro prediction unresolved.
A variant-overlapping PRRX1 peak in an adipose biosample would strengthen the PRRX1 chain relative to H5; its absence would not by itself rule out binding.
An adipose eQTL for this variant could provide context-matched genetic evidence for a target gene and help distinguish the proposed FTO link from alternatives.

critique.next_experiment: In an appropriate adipocyte-precursor model, create isogenic T/C alleles at the variant and measure allele-specific occupancy of the leading candidate TFs together with FTO expression; perturb the implicated enhancer or TF to test whether the allele-dependent expression effect is causal.
